input.quote: Customer agrees that, during the Term, Customer shall be required to obtain from M&I all of those Services which are included in the Monthly Base Fee, as set forth on Schedule 6.2.
input.rationale: § 10.3(A) imposes a sole-sourcing obligation on Customer: for the whole Term (defined in § 1.X as ending on the eighth anniversary of the Effective Date) Customer must obtain from M&I all Services included in the Monthly Base Fee, with no descope or partial-termination right and no exit tied to M&I's performance. That is exclusive dealing for the full term without a performance-based exit — walk-away territory — and it fails every fallback element other than arguably the defined category: the duration is eight years rather than 12 months, and nothing terminates the lock-in automatically on M&I's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates (§ 9 gives credits, and § 12 default remedies require a default and notice). The asymmetry is stark, since §§ 3.1-3.2 let M&I perform through Affiliates and third parties. Other "exclusive" hits are not Customer exclusivity: § 17.1 (our ownership of Customer Data), § 21.7(A), § 22 venue and § 23 licence grant; § 21.10 only sweeps in Affiliate processing "which M&I does" and imposes no sourcing obligation. We therefore replace the requirement with express freedom to source those Services from M&I or any other provider, meeting the preferred position.

mappings.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.

ops.oldText: Customer agrees that, during the Term, Customer shall be required to obtain from M&I all of those Services which are included in the Monthly Base Fee, as set forth on Schedule 6.2.
ops.newText: Customer may obtain those Services which are included in the Monthly Base Fee, as set forth on Schedule 6.2, from M&I or from any other provider, and shall have no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 10.3(A) locks us into obtaining all Monthly Base Fee Services from M&I for the entire eight-year Term with no performance-based exit, so we have replaced that requirement with express freedom to source those Services from M&I or any other provider. If M&I needs some protection, we could accept exclusivity confined to a defined service category for no more than 12 months, ending automatically on any failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.
proposal.summary: Remove Customer's Term-long sole-sourcing obligation in § 10.3(A)
